Class SlotClip

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.host.SlotClip
public final class SlotClip extends Object
Part of the created-slot contract, beside SlotScreenHook: a slot library tells MenuKit when an element places a slot, so the slot is clipped to what its panel shows of it (7.2.0).

A slot element writes its slot's position into Slot.x/y and vanilla draws and hit-tests the slot there, in its own slot pass. Inside a clipping container (a ScrollContainer's viewport, a Tabs body, or any element that scissors what it draws) a slot can sit across the clip's edge: the element's own frame is clipped like everything else it draws, but vanilla knows nothing of the clip. Calling shown(RenderContext, Slot) from the element's render, right after writing the position, hands MenuKit the clip in play. From then on:

  • vanilla's draw of the slot (item, count, durability, highlight) is clipped to it, so the part past the edge does not draw;
  • a point outside it neither hovers nor clicks the slot: it is the panel's, as a gap between slots is, so a carried item cannot drop through there either.
The slot keeps its real position, so nothing beside it moves. A slot wholly inside its clip looks and behaves exactly as before. One wholly outside should not be placed at all: a ScrollContainer does not render a child out of view, so its slot stays where its library parks it. Such a child gets PanelElement.renderCulled instead of render (7.4.0), so the element can tell a slot held out of view (park it) from one whose element is hidden.

  • Method Details

    • shown

      public static void shown(RenderContext ctx, net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot slot)
      Records that slot is placed this frame by an element rendering with ctx, under the clip that context draws in. Call once a frame for each slot placed, after writing its Slot.x/y; pass the slot that is in the screen's own menu.slots (on the creative screen, the wrapper around it), which is the one vanilla draws. Render thread only.

    • panelShowing

      public static boolean panelShowing(net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot slot)
      Whether the panel that last showed slot (shown(RenderContext, Slot)) was drawn this frame (7.3.0). Ask it at the end of the frame (SlotScreenHook.endFrame(AbstractContainerScreen)) for a slot that was not shown this frame, to tell why: true, its panel is on screen and the slot was scrolled out of view or hidden by its element, so park it; false, its panel is hidden or not on this screen (or no panel ever showed the slot), so a vanilla slot a panel took over goes back to its own place. Render thread only.

    • clipOf

      public static @Nullable Reference clipOf(net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot slot)
      The rectangle slot is shown within, in screen space (GUI pixels), or null when nothing clips it (7.4.0): what shown(RenderContext, Slot) was handed, every clipping ancestor's scissor intersected. A slot library can tell from it whether a slot is wholly in view, cut by a scroll edge, or out of it, say to hide a panel anchored on a slot whose slot is cut.

      It changes when the slot's element places it, with its Slot.x/y, so the two always agree: during a frame, before the element renders, it is last frame's; after, this frame's. A slot no panel showed last frame has none. Where two panels show one slot in a frame, it is the clip of the one on top. Render thread only.
